props.gloss_en: R' Yehuda: and logic decides [that it is the one] of the right
the mishna: [the sciatic-nerve prohibition applies] in the thigh of the left as well
it is obvious to R' Yehuda, and 'logic' means the logic of the Torah
he is in doubt, and 'logic' means that logic inclines [to the right]
the Pesachim mishna: the bones, the sinews and the leftover are burned on the sixteenth
Rav Chisda: [the sinews clause] is needed only for the gid hanasheh, according to R' Yehuda who says it applies only in one
Rav Ashi: it is needed only for its fat
the baraita: its fat is permitted, and holy Israel treated it as forbidden
Ravina: it is needed only [for the outer nerve], as Rav Yehuda said in Shmuel's name
Shmuel: there are two nerves -- the inner, next to the bone, is forbidden and one is liable for it
Shmuel: the outer, next to the flesh, is forbidden and one is not liable for it
the mishna: one who ate an olive-bulk from this and an olive-bulk from that incurs eighty lashes
R' Yehuda: he incurs only forty
and we have heard R' Yehuda say: an uncertain forewarning is not called a forewarning
the baraita's first tanna: [of two possible fathers] he struck this one and then that one, cursed this one and then that one, or struck or cursed both at once -- he is liable
R' Yehuda: [struck or cursed both] at once -- liable
R' Yehuda: one after the other -- exempt
this tanna holds like the other tanna of R' Yehuda, who said: an uncertain forewarning is called a forewarning
R' Yehuda: 'you shall not leave any of it until morning...' -- the verse gives a positive command after the prohibition, to say that one is not flogged for it
R' Yaakov: not for that reason, but because it is a prohibition without an act, and for any prohibition without an act one is not flogged
the baraita: one who ate two nerves from two thighs of two animals incurs eighty
R' Yehuda: he incurs only forty
since it says 'from two thighs of two animals', it is obvious both are forbidden, and [the case] was needed for R' Yehuda
here we are dealing with a case where [one nerve] has no olive-bulk
the baraita: one who ate it and it has no olive-bulk is liable
R' Yehuda: not until it has an olive-bulk
Rava: the verse says 'the thigh' -- the dominant one of the thighs
and the Rabbis: [the 'the' marks] the one whose prohibition spreads through the whole thigh, to exclude the outer [nerve], which does not
RYBL: the verse says 'as he wrestled with him' -- like a man hugging his fellow, whose hand reaches his fellow's right side
R' Shmuel bar Nachmani: [the angel] appeared to him as a gentile
a Jew joined by a gentile on the road keeps him to his right
Rava bar Ulla: he appeared to him as a Torah scholar
one who walks at his teacher's right is a boor
and the Rabbis: he came from behind him and struck him in both
the Rabbis need 'as he wrestled with him' for RYBL's other derasha
RYBL: this teaches that they raised the dust of their feet up to the Throne of Glory
RYBL: why is it called gid hanasheh? because it slipped (nasha) from its place and rose
and so it says: 'their might has failed (nashta), they became as women' (Jer 51:30)
R' Yosei b'R' Chanina: 'a word He sent against Jacob' (Isa 9:7) is the gid hanasheh; 'and it fell upon Israel' -- its prohibition spread through all Israel
R' Yosei b'R' Chanina: 'slaughter and prepare' (Gen 43:16) -- expose the place of slaughter to them; 'and prepare' -- remove the gid hanasheh before them
[this is] according to the one who says the gid hanasheh was forbidden to the Noahides
R' Elazar: 'and Jacob was left alone' (Gen 32:25) -- he stayed behind for small jars
R' Elazar: from here, the righteous hold their money dearer than their bodies -- and why so much? because they do not stretch out their hands to theft
R' Yitzchak: from here, a Torah scholar should not go out alone at night
R' Yitzchak's source: 'and a man wrestled with him until the rising of the dawn' (Gen 32:25)
R' Abba bar Kahana's source: 'behold, he winnows barley [tonight] at the threshing floor' (Ruth 3:2)
R' Abbahu's source: 'and Abraham rose early in the morning and saddled' (Gen 22:3)
the Rabbis' source: 'go now, see the welfare of your brothers' (Gen 37:14)
Rav's source: 'and the sun shone for him' (Gen 32:32)
it is written 'and the sun shone for him' (Gen 32:32) -- [read plainly: for him]
R' Yitzchak: the sun that set [early] for his sake shone [early] for his sake
R' Yitzchak (Gen 28:10-11): when he reached Haran and set his mind to return, the land contracted for him -- at once 'he came upon the place'
Jacob: is it possible that I passed the place where my fathers prayed and I did not pray?
the Holy One: this righteous man came to My lodging place, and shall he leave without staying the night?
R' Yitzchak: at once 'the sun had set' (Gen 28:11) -- [early, for him]
R' Yitzchak: 'he took of the stones of the place' (Gen 28:11) and 'he took the stone' (Gen 28:18) -- this teaches that all those stones gathered into one place
and each one said: upon me let this righteous man lay his head
a tanna taught: and all of them were absorbed into one
the tanna: how wide was the ladder? eight thousand parasangs
as it is written 'and behold angels of God ascending and descending on it' (Gen 28:12) -- ascending, two; descending, two; when they met they were four
and of an angel it is written 'his body was like Tarshish' (Dan 10:6), and it is learned [as tradition] that Tarshish is two thousand parasangs
the tanna: they ascended and gazed at his image above, and descended and gazed at his image below; they sought to endanger him -- at once 'and behold the Lord stood over him' (Gen 28:13)
Reish Lakish: were the verse not written, it could not be said -- like a man fanning his son
'the land on which you lie, to you I will give it' (Gen 28:13)
R' Yitzchak: this teaches that the Holy One folded all of Eretz Yisrael and set it under Jacob, so that it would be easy for his children to conquer
Jacob [to the angel]: are you a thief or a gambler, that you fear the dawn?
the angel: I am an angel, and from the day I was created my time to say song has not come until now
Rav (as first reported): three groups of ministering angels say song every day: one says 'holy', one says 'holy', and one says 'holy is the Lord of hosts'
the baraita: Israel are dearer before the Holy One than the ministering angels -- Israel say song at every hour, and the angels only once a day
and some say once a week; some say once a month; some once a year; some once in seven years; some once a jubilee; some once in the world's history
the baraita: Israel mention the Name after two words ('Hear, Israel, the Lord'); the ministering angels mention the Name only after three words ('holy, holy, holy, the Lord of hosts')
as it is said: 'Hear, Israel: the Lord...' (Deut 6:4)
as it is written: 'holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts' (Isa 6:3)
the baraita: the ministering angels do not say song above until Israel say it below
as it is said: 'when the morning stars sang together', and only then 'and all the sons of God shouted' (Job 38:7)
rather [Rav said]: one says 'holy', one says 'holy, holy', and one says 'holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts'
'he strove with an angel and prevailed' (Hos 12:5) -- I do not know who became master of whom; ... you must say Jacob became master over the angel
when it says 'for you have striven with God [angels]' (Gen 32:29)
'he wept and made supplication to him' -- I do not know who wept to whom; ... you must say the angel wept to Jacob
when it says 'and he said: let me go' (Gen 32:27)
Rabba: [the angel] hinted to him that two princes would issue from him -- the Exilarch in Babylonia and the Nasi in Eretz Yisrael; from here he hinted exile to him

Rav: 'and in the vine were three branches' (Gen 40:10) -- these are three proud princes who issue from Israel in every generation, sometimes two here and one in Eretz Yisrael, sometimes two there and one here
the Rabbis set their eyes on Rabbana Ukva and Rabbana Nechemya, the sons of Rav's daughter
Rava: these are three princes of the nations, who plead in Israel's favour in every generation
R' Eliezer: 'vine' is the world; 'three branches' Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; 'as it budded its blossoms shot forth' the matriarchs; 'its clusters ripened into grapes' the tribes
R' Yehoshua: rather, 'vine' is the Torah; 'three branches' Moses, Aaron and Miriam; 'budded' the Sanhedrin; 'ripened grapes' the righteous of every generation
Rabban Gamliel: we still need the Modai, who sets the whole of it in one place
R' Elazar HaModai: 'vine' is Jerusalem; 'three branches' the Temple, the king and the High Priest; 'budded' the young priests; 'ripened grapes' the libations
RYBL (reading it of the gifts): 'vine' is the Torah; 'three branches' the well, the pillar of cloud and the manna; 'budded' the first fruits; 'ripened grapes' the libations

R' Yirmeya bar Abba: 'vine' is Israel; 'three branches' the three pilgrimage festivals; 'as it budded' Israel's time to be fruitful and multiply; 'its blossoms shot forth' Israel's time to be redeemed; 'ripened grapes' Egypt's time to drink the cup of fury
and so it says: 'You brought a vine out of Egypt' (Ps 80:9)
and so it says: 'and the children of Israel were fruitful and swarmed' (Ex 1:7)
and so it says: 'their lifeblood (nitzcham) is spattered on My garments, and I have stained (egalti) all My raiment' (Isa 63:3)
Rava: why are three cups stated of Egypt? one it drank in Moses' days, one in the days of Pharaoh Nekho, and one it will drink with all the nations
Reish Lakish: this nation is likened to a vine -- its branches the householders, its clusters the Torah scholars, its leaves the unlearned, its tendrils the empty ones of Israel
[sent from Eretz Yisrael:] let the clusters pray for the leaves, for were it not for the leaves the clusters would not survive
R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak: 'so I bought her (va'ekreha) for fifteen [pieces] of silver' (Hos 3:2) -- kira is nothing but the language of sale
as it is said: 'in my grave which I bought (kariti) for myself' (Gen 50:5)
R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak: 'fifteen' is the fifteenth of Nisan, when Israel were redeemed from Egypt; 'silver' -- these are the righteous
and so it says: 'he has taken the bag of silver with him' (Prov 7:20)
R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak: 'a chomer of barley and a letech of barley' -- these are the forty-five righteous by whom the world endures
and I do not know whether thirty are here and fifteen in Eretz Yisrael, or the reverse; ... you must say: thirty in Eretz Yisrael and fifteen here
when it says 'and I took the thirty [pieces] of silver and cast them into the house of the Lord, to the treasury' (Zech 11:13)
Abaye: and most of them are found in the synagogue under the upper room (tutei apta)
and that is what is written: 'and I said to them: if it is good in your eyes, give me my hire ... and they weighed my hire, thirty [pieces] of silver' (Zech 11:12)
R' Yehuda: these are thirty righteous of the nations of the world, by whom the nations endure
Ulla: these are thirty commandments the Noahides accepted, of which they keep only three
Ulla: one, that they do not write a marriage contract for males; one, that they do not weigh the flesh of the dead in the butcher-shops; and one, that they honour the Torah

deflected_by.gloss_en: לעולם אימא לך מיפשט פשיטא ליה, והכא במאי עסקינן -- כשהוכרו ולבסוף נתערבו
רב אשי אמר: לא נצרכה אלא לשמנו -- the mishna's sinews are not the gid hanasheh at all, so nothing follows about R' Yehuda (= p_rav_ashi_shamno)
רבינא אמר: לא נצרכה אלא לכדרב יהודה אמר שמואל -- the outer nerve, forbidden without liability (= p_ravina_chitzon)

supports.gloss_en: ת״ש: מזה כזית ומזה כזית -- R' Yehuda: forty. אי אמרת בשלמא מיפשט פשיטא ליה, שפיר; אלא אי אמרת ספוקי מספקא ליה -- הויא לה התראת ספק, and R' Yehuda holds uncertain forewarning is no forewarning (91a.4)

deflected_by.gloss_en: האי תנא סבר לה כאידך תנא דרבי יהודה, דאמר התראת ספק שמה התראה (= p_ry_hatraat_safek_hatraa)

supports.gloss_en: ת״ש: two nerves from two thighs of two animals -- R' Yehuda: forty; מדקאמר משתי ירכות משתי בהמות, פשיטא דתרוייהו לאיסורא, ולרבי יהודה איצטריך -- שמע מינה מיפשט פשיטא ליה (91a.10)
דתניא: שמנו מותר, וישראל קדושים נהגו בו איסור
כדרב יהודה אמר שמואל: the outer nerve, next to the flesh, is forbidden and one is not liable for it
דתניא: R' Yehuda -- [struck or cursed the two possible fathers] at once, liable; one after the other, exempt
דתניא: ״לא תותירו ממנו עד בקר״ -- an aseh after the lav, so no lashes, the words of R' Yehuda; R' Yaakov: because it is a lav without an act
דתניא: אכלו ואין בו כזית -- חייב; רבי יהודה אומר: עד שיהא בו כזית
וטעמא מאי? אמר רבא: אמר קרא ״הירך״ -- המיומנת שבירך
אמר קרא ״בהאבקו עמו״ -- כאדם שחובק את חבירו, וידו מגעת לכף ימינו של חבירו
כגוי נדמה לו -- [so Jacob kept him at his right]
דאמר מר: ישראל שנטפל לו גוי בדרך -- טופלו לימינו
כתלמיד חכם נדמה לו -- [so Jacob walked at his left]
דאמר מר: המהלך לימין רבו -- הרי זה בור
וכן הוא אומר: ״נשתה גבורתם היו לנשים״
כמאן דאמר גיד הנשה נאסר לבני נח -- the stam places R' Yosei b'R' Chanina's reading within that view
מכאן -- from his staying behind for small jars
״ויאבק איש עמו עד עלות השחר״ -- מכאן לתלמיד חכם שלא יצא יחידי בלילה
רבי אבא בר כהנא אמר מהכא: ״הנה הוא זרה את גרן השערים [הלילה]״
רבי אבהו אמר מהכא: ״וישכם אברהם בבקר״
ורבנן אמרי מהכא: ״לך נא ראה את שלום אחיך״
רב אמר מהכא: ״ויזרח לו השמש״
דכתיב ״עולים ויורדים בו״ -- two ascending and two descending, four where they meet
וכתיב ״וגויתו כתרשיש״, וגמירי דתרשיש תרי אלפי פרסי -- four times two thousand
מסייע ליה לרב חננאל אמר רב -- the angel's 'my time to say song has not come until now'
שנאמר ״שמע ישראל ה׳״ ... כדכתיב ״קדוש קדוש קדוש ה׳ צבאות״
שנאמר ״ברן יחד כוכבי בקר״ והדר ״ויריעו כל בני אלהים״
כשהוא אומר ״כי שרית עם אלהים״ -- הוי אומר יעקב נעשה שר למלאך
כשהוא אומר ״ויאמר שלחני״ -- הוי אומר מלאך בכה ליעקב
עדיין צריכין אנו למודעי, דמוקים ליה כוליה בחד מקום
וכן הוא אומר: ״גפן ממצרים תסיע״
וכן הוא אומר: ״ובני ישראל פרו וישרצו״
וכן הוא אומר: ״ויז נצחם על בגדי וכל מלבושי אגאלתי״

והיינו דשלחו מתם: ליבעי רחמים איתכליא על עליא
שנאמר ״בקברי אשר כריתי לי״
וכן הוא אומר: ״צרור הכסף לקח בידו״
כשהוא אומר ״ואקחה שלשים הכסף ואשליך אתו בית ה׳״ -- הוי אומר שלשים בארץ ישראל

objections.gloss_en: והוינן בה: הני גידי מאי עבידתייהו? if sinews of meat, let him eat them; if leftover, that is notar; rather neck sinews -- if they are not meat, let him throw them away!

answered_by.gloss_en: לא נצרכה אלא לגיד הנשה, ואליבא דרבי יהודה (= p_rav_chisda_gid_hanasheh)

objections.gloss_en: ואי פשיטא ליה, אמאי סופג ארבעים ותו לא? לילקי שמונים! -- if it is obvious to him [and both nerves are forbidden], why forty and no more?

answered_by.gloss_en: הכא במאי עסקינן -- כגון דלית ביה כזית (= p_okimta_leit_bei_kezayit), and R' Yehuda holds one is not liable without an olive-bulk

objections.gloss_en: ורבנן, האי ״בהאבקו עמו״ מאי דרשי ביה? -- what do the Rabbis, who forbid the left thigh too, do with the verse RYBL reads as the right?

answered_by.gloss_en: מבעי ליה לכאידך דרבי יהושע בן לוי -- the dust that rose to the Throne of Glory (= p_rabbanan_behaavko_mibaei)

objections.gloss_en: וכי שמש לו לבד זרחה? והלא לכל העולם זרחה! -- asked of Rabban Gamliel and R' Yehoshua in the market of Emmaus

answered_by.gloss_en: שמש הבאה בעבורו זרחה בעבורו (= p_shemesh_habaa_baavuro)

objections.gloss_en: מיתיבי: the ministering angels mention the Name only after three words -- but in Rav's version the third group says it after one 'kadosh'
והאיכא ״ברוך״! -- 'blessed is the glory of the Lord' (Ezek 3:12) mentions the Name after fewer than three words

answered_by.gloss_en: ״ברוך״ -- אופנים הוא דאמרי ליה -- it is the ofanim who say it, not the ministering angels
ואיבעית אימא: כיון דאתיהיב רשותא, אתיהיב -- once permission is given [after three words], it is given

objections.gloss_en: וכי מראין לו לאדם מה שהיה? והלא אין מראין לו לאדם אלא מה שעתיד להיות! -- R' Eliezer's patriarchs, matriarchs and tribes were already past
